claims.text: MoNbTaW is a body-centered-cubic refractory high-entropy alloy.
HfNbTaTiZr can serve as a single-phase bcc refractory high-entropy alloy in a disordered solid-solution state.
Refractory high-entropy alloys can have a significant energetic driving force for chemical short-range order.
Controlled annealing or rapid quenching can tune SRO clusters from isolated clusters to a connected, percolating network.
The relevant single-phase bcc alloy is thermodynamically stable above 0.5 Tm.
Negative mixing enthalpy for selected elemental pairs promotes SRO while the potential-energy surface can simultaneously prevent long-range phase decomposition.
Isolated SRO clusters act as strong point-defect-like phonon-scattering centers and reduce thermal conductivity.
Percolating SRO clusters alter the local vibrational density of states.
A connected SRO network creates coherent, low-disorder phonon-transport pathways with a reduced effective disorder potential.
Crossing the SRO percolation threshold enhances or sustains thermal conductivity relative to the isolated-cluster regime.
Thermal conductivity varies non-monotonically with SRO fraction, first decreasing and then plateauing or increasing at high SRO fraction.
The conductivity-versus-SRO curve has an inflection point corresponding to the SRO percolation threshold.
Above the percolation threshold, conductivity is higher than predicted by standard scattering or serial/parallel mixing models at the same degree of ordering.
Standard effective-medium and serial/parallel mixing models treat the effect of SRO fraction as linear or additive and predict a monotonic conductivity decrease.
Standard interatomic potentials often fail to predict SRO evolution, cluster size, and connectivity accurately.
A highly accurate machine-learning interatomic potential can represent SRO effects in a bcc MoNbTaW RHEA.

Chemical ordering in multicomponent alloys can drive transitions from disordered structures toward distinct crystalline or intermetallic states, so phase decomposition is a relevant boundary condition.
The exact percolation threshold and conductivity change depend on atomic-size mismatch and the accuracy of the machine-learning potential.
